title: Temp File Name Collision Returned to the Caller
pattern: A temporary-file helper takes or derives a fixed name and returns `AlreadyExists` on collision, instead of generating unique names itself until creation succeeds.
why_bad: The caller wants a fresh unique file, not a specific name. Surfacing the collision pushes a retry-with-new-name loop onto every caller, and the typical `exists()` then `create()` sequence races with other processes: it can also silently truncate a file created in between.
detection: A temp or scratch file creation helper that returns an error when the path exists and contains no loop generating alternative random names with atomic `create_new(true)` (or `O_EXCL`), and does not delegate to a temp-file facility such as the `tempfile` crate or `mkstemp`.
counterexample: Creation at a deterministic path the caller specifically requires, such as a lock file, a PID file or a content-addressed artifact, where a collision is meaningful.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Chapter 8; John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 10.
